artifacts.summary: Weighs one Modal family against a separate Stability family; recommends keeping one family, understood as necessity operators parameterized by operator, with three record amendments; includes the Open/Nomic instance analysis, the cslib hosting review, and the full change list for the contrary ruling.

memory_candidates.content: BimodalLogic necessity operators form one parameterized family. Box, stab (L-plus), ofut and opast (Open language) are each S5 with K/T/4/5 as axioms and necessitation derived through the inclusion chain box => stab => ofut/opast. Each restricted necessity carries a rigid class on which phi -> N phi holds and outside which uniform substitution fails: state-local formulas for stab, pure-past for ofut, pure-future for opast; atoms are in all three. The nomic operator is only KD over arbitrary nomic frames (T needs Lawful, 4 needs Uniform over integer time, S5 holds on the tense-free fragment). Interactions with Temporal are operator-specific and share no statement: MF/TF/perpetuity for box, pasting for stab, HN for the open modals.

cslib's modal axiom classes and Modal*Hilbert bundles take [HasBox F] as an instance ARGUMENT, not a field, so they are already parameterized by the box operator at the type level; a second necessity operator on one formula type can be hosted without changing cslib by an explicit non-canonical HasBox instance, a type synonym, or a ProofSigHom sending box to the second operator. cslib's own precedent for a second necessity-like operator (G/H in BimodalTMHilbert) is operator-specific axiom classes, not a second HasBox.
